column1: BharatTrip - Refund Operations Data Extract
Extract window: 1 February 2026 to 30 June 2026. Snapshot taken 30 June 2026.
This workbook contains anonymised operational data from a B2B travel company's
refund process. When a travel agent cancels a booking they request a refund.
Two teams touch every refund:
- The Support team talks to agents and logs each request in 'Support_Tracker'.
- The Finance team actually pays the money out and logs it in 'Finance_Tracker'.
Each team maintains its own sheet, in its own way. Column names and conventions
differ between them. The two sheets are supposed to describe the same refunds,
but they were built independently and were never reconciled. Working out how
they relate to each other is part of the task.
TAB: Support_Tracker
One row per refund request as logged by Support. 'Refund Amount (INR)' is the
amount recorded against the request. 'Status' values are set by Support and mean
whatever the individual agent took them to mean. 'Channel' is how the request
reached us. 'Handled By' is the Support person who owns the ticket.
TAB: Finance_Tracker
One row per refund Finance was made aware of. 'Amount Paid (INR)' is what actually
left the account. 'Received On' is when Finance says the request reached them.
'Approved By' is only filled in where a sign-off happened.
TAB: Escalations
Complaints logged against refunds. The escalation log was only started on
1 March 2026, so nothing before that date appears here. 'Days Open' is measured
to the resolution date, or to the 30 June snapshot if still open.
Known limitations of this extract (stated plainly, not fixed):
- Some refund requests arrive by email or messaging app and are never logged.
- Dates were hand-typed in places, so some cells are text rather than dates.
- Agent names were free-typed and are not spelled consistently.
- Rows have occasionally been pasted twice.
No other documentation exists. There is no process manual, no SLA document and no
written refund policy in circulation. If you need to make an assumption, write it down.
